tnn.review: Tnn is good and such a good person. Take regular notes and follow her instructions. Report presentation ar case study te ektu pera dibe so be sure to create a good team For exam(broad questions) be sure to write as she instructs also make sure to add examples

Tnn - MGT351
This is my 2nd course under Tnn and it saddens me that I won't get a third to do under her. She's probably the most standard faculty I've come across so far ; strict but only as much as she needs to be. She won't do you outstanding favors but she won't make your lives miserable either. In order to do well, you have to attend classes regularly and engage as much as you can. The questions in the exam are very standard I would say ; Easy if you're up to date with your studies. Nothing ever comes outside of the slides and she provides suggestions before the exam. She takes 2 quizzes (;est 1) worth 10 marks, a case study, 1 mid (25 marks) report + presentation (20 marks) and final exam (30 marks) she might be very picky when it comes to answers in the exams. Writing too much might get your marks deducted. She too prefers writing to the very point ; only as much as you need. If you're the kind of person that has a "bujhaye likhe dibo" tendency, think twice. You can write your ideas around the main topic keeping them central but not the other way around. This will get you negative marking. And she is really strict when it comes to presentation. Each group will get no longer than 10 minutes and there will be a lot of questions after the presentation from the faculty. If you know what is written on the report, you'll be able to answer or else no. The questions are pretty straightforward. But, she grades fairly and curves depending on the overall performance of the section (Curves mostly from what I've seen) A factor to consider would be : Cracking A/A- under Tnn is very easy if you're regular. But, if you're somebody that misses classes and has no clue about what's going on in the class, you're not even gonna get a B. (Just wanted to flex that all 6 members from my group got 4As and 2A-s ; if you think there was nepotism involved, WRONG. This is how easy it is when you're regular)
